answer: Under a quadratic slashing gale, each Sybil cluster must lock collateral C(n)=κn², so marginal attack cost grows 2κn per added identity while extractable value stays linear, forcing any rational wander across identities to lose. Juniper commitments deepen this: liquidity-sink lockups impose opportunity costs above κn², capping extraction at V<0.5κn² and sustaining a consensus threshold where attack cost exceeds value.
